hypotheses.text: Karayol-Borroto-Haghshenas neurodevelopmental syndrome (MSL2) exhibits a significantly higher prevalence of autism spectrum disorder behaviors (~64%) compared to MSL3-related Basilicata-Akhtar syndrome and KAT8-related disorders, distinguishing it clinically within MSL complex chromatinopathies.
hypotheses.rationale: Comparative phenotypic analyses of epigenetic chromatin-modifying complex disorders indicate that while global developmental delay and hypotonia are shared across MSL2, MSL3, and KAT8, behavioral profiles diverge, with autism-like phenotypes disproportionately enriched in MSL2 cohorts.

evidence.text: Comparative analysis across MSL complex disorders demonstrated autism spectrum disorder features in 64.3% of individuals harboring MSL2 variants, contrasting with distinct variant phenotypic manifestations in MSL3.

hypotheses.text: A specific machine-learning peripheral blood DNA methylation episignature achieves complete classification separation (MVP score near 1.0) between MSL2-related neurodevelopmental disorder and MSL3-related Basilicata-Akhtar syndrome / KAT8-related syndromes.
hypotheses.rationale: Because bulk histone acetylation (H4K16ac) remains unchanged in MSL2 deficiency unlike in MSL3 and KAT8/MOF defects, downstream epigenomic consequences alter distinct DNA methylation loci, allowing a support vector machine (SVM) classifier to differentiate MSL2 from other MSL/NSL complex disorders with high specificity.

evidence.text: A sensitive and specific DNA methylation episignature model generates MVP classification scores ranging from 0 to 1, distinguishing MSL2 syndrome cases clearly from Basilicata-Akhtar syndrome (MSL3) and controls.

hypotheses.text: Motor deficits in MSL2 syndrome are predominantly characterized by truncal/gait coordination ataxia and feeding difficulties rather than early intractable epilepsy or severe spasticity seen in KAT8- or severe MSL3-related presentations.
hypotheses.rationale: Motor manifestations are present in a large majority of MSL2 patients, but seizures affect only a minority (<30%), establishing lack of motor coordination and gait disturbance as the predominant motor hallmarks relative to active epileptic encephalopathy.

evidence.text: MSL2 variants are consistently associated with motor issues such as coordination problems, feeding difficulties, and gait disturbance, whereas seizures occur to a lesser extent.

new_directions.question_text: What specific differentially methylated probe sets (CpG loci) in the MSL2 peripheral blood episignature show zero overlap or inverse methylation directionality compared to Basilicata-Akhtar syndrome (MSL3)?
new_directions.rationale: Delineating the specific CpGs that differentiate MSL2 from MSL3 episignatures will enable precise single-locus or targeted panel diagnostics when exome variants of uncertain significance (VUS) are encountered.

new_directions.question_text: How do quantitative dysmorphic facial metrics (using 3D photogrammetry/GestaltMatcher) differentiate Karayol-Borroto-Haghshenas syndrome probands from MSL3 and KAT8-related syndromes?
new_directions.rationale: MSL2 probands have recognizable facial dysmorphisms, but distinguishing them from other MSL/NSL complex disorders based purely on non-automated dysmorphology is challenging due to overlapping facial traits.
